# New renderings for iliad-064 (Iliad 11.1–121)

No departure from a published Odyssey or Iliad rendering. Published English was reused for 11.1 (Odyssey dawn-line, whose Greek differs only in ὄρνυθ’ / βροτοῖσι), 11.5–9 (8.222–224, with "she" for Strife), 11.13–14, 11.17–18, 11.41–42 (5.743; the helmet lines of 3.336–337 and the Odyssey), 11.43, 11.82, 11.84–85 and the formulae θεὸς ὣς τίετο δήμῳ, διὰ δρυμὰ πυκνὰ καὶ ὕλην, νώροπα χαλκόν, ἄσβεστος (table), ἄληκτον (table: "unrelenting" / "relentless").

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἔνθα στᾶσ’ ἤϋσε θεὰ μέγα τε δεινόν τε ὄρθι’ (11.10–11, whole-line sense; the first half follows 5.784 "took her stand and shouted") | "there, having stood, she shouted, the goddess, greatly and fearsomely, high-pitched," | "and there the goddess took her stand and shouted, greatly and fearsomely, in a high-pitched voice," | "terribly", "dreadfully" (δεινόν is "fearsomely" as at the table's δεινὸν δὲ λόφος καθύπερθεν ἔνευεν); "upright", "straight up" for ὄρθια (the literal word; of a voice it is taken as "high, shrill", and the note says so) |
| βλοσυρῶπις (Γοργώ, 11.36; βλοσυρός sense not certain) | "grim-faced" | "grim-faced" (+ note: meaning of βλοσυρός not certain, "grim" the usual guess) | "fierce-eyed", "grim-eyed", "terrible-eyed", "shaggy-faced" (each decides the unknown); "fearsome" is kept for δεινόν |
| οὔλιος ἀστήρ (11.62) | "fatal" | "fatal" | "baneful" (ὀλοός), "ruinous" (οὐλόμενος), "destructive", "deadly" (all taken by the table for other words), "evil-boding" (adds an omen the Greek does not state) |
| κραταιός (κραταιοῦ θηρός, 11.119) | "powerful" | "powerful" | "mighty" (ἴφθιμος), "strong" (κρατερός), "stout" (στιβαρός) |
| ἠῶθι πρό (11.50) | "early in the morning" | "in the early morning" (+ note: force of πρό not clear) | "before dawn", "at first light", "at daybreak" (each decides the unclear πρό) |
| ἴσας … κεφαλὰς ἔχεν (ὑσμίνη, 11.72; an idiom, the exact picture not known) | "equal heads the battle held" | "the battle held their heads level" (+ note: usual sense "kept the sides level"; picture not known) | "kept the fight even", "fought on equal terms" (loses κεφαλάς and decides the idiom) |
| πολύστονος (Ἔρις, 11.73) | "much-groaning" | "of the many groans" (+ note: for Strife "causing many groans") | "grief-bringing", "tearful", "full of lament" (each decides whose groans); follows the Odyssey's πολύστονος "much-groaning" / "of many groans" |
| λάμφ’ ὥς τε στεροπὴ πατρὸς Διὸς αἰγιόχοιο (11.66, whole line; the line without αἰγιόχοιο is already shipped at 10.154) | "all in bronze he shone like the lightning of father Zeus, aegis-bearing" | "and he shone all over in his bronze, like the lightning of aegis-bearing father Zeus" | "flashed", "gleamed" (λάμπω is "shone", as shipped), "thunderbolt" (στεροπή is the flash, κεραυνός the bolt) |
| ἄνδρα Βιάνορα ποιμένα λαῶν αὐτόν (11.92–93; αὐτόν "Bianor himself" against his companion) | "a man, Bianor, shepherd of the people, himself" | "killed Bianor, shepherd of the people" (+ note on αὐτόν) | "Bianor himself" in `i` (stresses what the Greek only contrasts), "the leader" (ποιμὴν λαῶν is the table's "shepherd of the people") |
| νόθον καὶ γνήσιον (11.102) | "one a bastard and one true-born" | "one illegitimate and one legitimate" | "base-born" and "natural" (νόθος is "bastard" / "illegitimate" as in the table), "lawfully born", "genuine" for γνήσιος; the pair keeps the table's νόθος and gives γνήσιος "true-born" in `l`, "legitimate" in `i` |
